label: Entered Cambridge to study mathematics
description: Brenda entered Cambridge in 1936 to study mathematics but later switched to psychology.

sources.quote: Brenda entered Cambridge in 1936 to study mathematics but later switched to psychology.

label: Worked in a radar establishment
description: During World War II she worked in a radar establishment before moving to Montreal.

sources.quote: During World War II she worked in a radar establishment before moving to Montreal in 1944 with her husband, Peter Milner

label: Moved to Montreal
description: Moved to Montreal in 1944 with her husband, Peter Milner, who was unexpectedly suddenly sent there to help set up Canadian atomic-energy research.

sources.quote: moving to Montreal in 1944 with her husband, Peter Milner, who was unexpectedly suddenly sent there to help set up Canadian atomic-energy research.

label: Got job at University of Montreal
description: She got a job at the University of Montreal teaching psychology and animal behavior (in French).

sources.quote: She got a job at the University of Montreal teaching psychology and animal behavior (in French).

label: Began graduate work at McGill
description: Following the war she began graduate work at McGill with Donald Hebb.

sources.quote: Following the war she began graduate work at McGill with Donald Hebb.

label: Began working with Penfield's patients
description: Brenda began working with Wilder Penfield's neurosurgical patients in 1950 where she studied the role of the temporal lobes in visual perception and memory for her Ph.D.

sources.quote: Brenda began working with Wilder Penfield's neurosurgical patients in 1950 where she studied the role of the temporal lobes in visual perception and memory for her Ph.D.

label: Published classic study of patient H.M.
description: This opportunity led to Brenda's now classic studies of patient H.M (Scoville and Milner, 1957).

sources.quote: This opportunity led to Brenda's now classic studies of patient H.M (Scoville and Milner, 1957).

label: Attended Frontal Granular Cortex symposium
description: Brenda Milner's opportunity to introduce her work on frontal lobe came at a large symposium on the Frontal Granular Cortex and Behavior held at Pennsylvania State University in 1962.

sources.quote: Brenda Milner's opportunity to introduce her work on frontal lobe came at a large symposium on the Frontal Granular Cortex and Behavior held at Pennsylvania State University in 1962

label: Published chapter on frontal lobectomy
description: Milner's chapter, "Some effects of frontal lobectomy in man," was the ﬁrst systematic study of the effect of frontal lobe excisions on cognition in human patients.

sources.quote: Milner's chapter, "Some effects of frontal lobectomy in man," was the ﬁrst systematic study of the effect of frontal lobe excisions on cognition in human patients.

label: Published design fluency study
description: A study devised by Jones-Gotman and Milner (1977) showed that right frontal lobe patients were impaired at a non-verbal analog of verbal fluency.

sources.quote: A study devised by Jones-Gotman and Milner (1977) showed that right frontal lobe patients were impaired at a non-verbal analog of verbal fluency.

label: Published movement copying study
description: Kolb and Milner (1981) asked patients to copy a series of arm or facial movements.

sources.quote: Kolb and Milner (1981) asked patients to copy a series of arm or facial movements (see Figure 3 ).

label: Published associative learning study
description: Finally, a series of studies by Milner and Petrides (1984) and Petrides (1985, 1990, 1997) demonstrated a severe impairment on conditional associative tasks.

sources.quote: Finally, a series of studies by Milner and Petrides (1984) and Petrides (1985, 1990, 1997) demonstrated a severe impairment on conditional associative tasks requiring the learning of arbitrary associations between a set of stimuli and a set of responses.

label: Published recency memory study
description: The sequencing deﬁcit could also be interpreted as a deﬁcit in the temporal organization of behavior as later shown by Milner et al. (1991).

sources.quote: The sequencing deﬁcit could also be interpreted as a deﬁcit in the temporal organization of behavior as later shown by Milner et al. (1991).
